outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a read of the public data and news above, meant to help you decide, not a recommendation. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: AI-monetizing software, led by Microsoft's earnings beat
strongest.reason: Microsoft surged about 15% on strong Azure growth and AI-capex commentary, while Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Adobe all extended recent gains on similar AI-monetization data points — ServiceNow raised guidance after a strong Q2 and CrowdStrike continues to outperform in the ongoing cybersecurity earnings window.

strongest.area: Crypto stabilizing after the Fed decision
strongest.reason: Bitcoin and Ethereum both firmed once the Fed held rates steady in a 9-3 vote, removing a key source of near-term uncertainty even though both remain well off recent highs.

weakest.reason: AMD, Micron, ASML, and Arm all fell sharply as the broader semiconductor complex has now shed roughly $1.3 trillion in value since last Friday, driven by renewed doubts about AI-capex sustainability and reports of Chinese progress in advanced chipmaking; Arm fell despite an outright earnings beat, underscoring how stretched sentiment has become in the group.

weakest.area: Meta and the AI-spending side of the ledger
weakest.reason: Meta dropped roughly 9.7% on disappointing guidance and a steep cashflow decline tied to AI spending, extending an 11-day losing streak — a sharp contrast to Microsoft's reaction and a reminder that the market is now discriminating hard between AI spenders and AI monetizers.

outlook.nextStep: The clearest, most dated signal today is the split between Microsoft's blowout Azure/AI-monetization beat and Meta's guidance-driven slide — worth a closer look at what's actually converting AI spend into revenue versus what isn't. The broader chip-sector selloff and Arm's post-earnings drop despite a beat are noisier, sentiment-driven moves that are better watched than acted on until they settle.

signals.title: Fed holds rates in a rare 9-3 split vote, Warsh's first meeting as chair
signals.body: The FOMC kept rates at 3.50-3.75% for a fifth straight meeting, but three officials dissented in favor of a hike — one of the closest votes in years. New Chair Kevin Warsh kept his press-conference remarks unusually brief, saying he "asked for a good family fight, and I got one." Markets trimmed September hike odds from roughly 79% to 60% following the announcement.
signals.watch: Whether the 3-person dissent becomes a larger bloc at the next meeting, and how Warsh's shorter communication style evolves.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — a genuinely divided vote under new leadership is a more informative signal about the path ahead than a unanimous hold would have been.

signals.title: Microsoft jumps 15% while Meta sinks 9.7% — the AI trade splits sharply on earnings
signals.body: Microsoft surged after beating on Azure growth and AI-capex commentary. Meta moved the opposite direction, missing on EPS ($6.18 vs. $7.22 expected), guiding revenue below consensus, and reporting a 91% drop in cashflow tied to AI spending — extending an 11-day losing streak, its longest on record, with more than ten brokerages cutting price targets.
signals.watch: Whether Amazon's upcoming earnings land closer to Microsoft's monetization story or Meta's spending-concern story.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — two mega-cap AI spenders reporting on the same day with opposite reactions is a concrete data point on which AI investments are showing returns.

signals.title: Semiconductor selloff deepens: sector has shed roughly $1.3 trillion since last Friday
signals.body: Chip stocks extended a multi-day rout, with Micron and SK Hynix both down over 8%, Intel down nearly 6%, and AMD down roughly 8% at its lows, while Korean and Samsung shares fell double digits overseas. Separately, Arm beat Q1 estimates (record $1.29B revenue, EPS of $0.45 vs. $0.37 expected, data-center royalty revenue more than doubling) but still fell as smartphone-market deceleration and a rich valuation overshadowed the beat.
signals.watch: Whether the selloff is a valuation reset after an exceptional rally, as some analysts argue, or an early sign of softening AI demand.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — a broad, multi-day, cross-border rout with a beat-and-drop reaction sitting inside it is more consistent with a sentiment repricing than a single clean catalyst.

signals.title: Humanoid-robot component names keep drawing bid, Teradyne holds most of its earnings pop
signals.body: Component makers tied to humanoid robotics — including lidar, vision-processing, and motor names — have rallied sharply in recent sessions on the thesis that any acceleration in humanoid build rates lifts the whole component tier at once, since these suppliers sell into multiple robot manufacturers simultaneously. Teradyne is holding most of its 12.8% post-earnings gain from its Q2 beat and raised guidance.
signals.watch: Whether upcoming earnings from other component suppliers corroborate the demand thesis with hard numbers, the way Teradyne's did.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — a supply-chain-wide rally with a specific, dated earnings beat inside it is more grounded than sentiment alone.

signals.title: Enterprise software extends its AI-monetization rally as cybersecurity earnings season kicks off
signals.body: Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Adobe all posted solid gains, with ServiceNow raising guidance after a strong Q2. In the adjacent cybersecurity group, Fortinet jumped over 12% on a billings beat and Qualys topped estimates, with Zscaler, Check Point, and Fortinet's earnings all landing within the same three-day window — a concentrated test of whether the sector's rich valuations are justified.
signals.watch: Zscaler and Check Point's upcoming results as the next data points in the same theme.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — multiple companies posting similar AI-monetization and billings beats in the same week looks like a real trend rather than noise.

signals.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum firm up after the Fed's hold
signals.body: Bitcoin rose back above $64,800 and Ethereum moved above $1,920 as the Fed's decision to hold rates removed a source of near-term uncertainty. Both remain down noticeably from recent highs, and separate reports flagged a crypto exchange cutting 20% of staff and a securities-fraud case in Thailand tied to a 2021 exchange hack — reminders that sector-specific risk hasn't gone away even as the macro backdrop eases.
signals.watch: Whether the post-Fed bounce holds through the next few sessions or fades as it has after prior rate decisions.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — a relief bounce tied to a single macro event is a weaker signal than a move driven by crypto-specific news.

signals.title: Cybersecurity sector earnings season underway, Fortinet leads with a strong beat
signals.body: Fortinet jumped more than 12% on second-quarter billings that beat estimates, and Qualys also topped revenue expectations. CrowdStrike continues to outperform peers this year (+46% YTD vs. Zscaler's -44.5%), while Zscaler, Check Point, and Fortinet's results all land within days of each other, giving the market a concentrated read on whether the group's premium valuations (average P/E near 90) hold up.
signals.watch: Zscaler's own earnings report, due within days, as the next test for a name that's lagged CrowdStrike sharply this year.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — a cluster of same-week earnings reports in one sector is one of the more dated, verifiable signals available right now.
